name: Portland
summary: New England's best small food city — a working waterfront, cobblestone Old Port, lighthouses, and lobster every which way.

lodging.name: The Press Hotel
lodging.blurb: A boutique hotel in the former Portland Press Herald building — central to the Old Port.

foodMustTry.name: Lobster roll at Eventide Oyster Co.
foodMustTry.blurb: The brown-butter lobster roll on a steamed bun that reset the standard.

foodMustTry.name: A Holy Donut potato doughnut
foodMustTry.blurb: Maine potato in the dough makes them absurdly good.

days.label: Day 25 — Old Port & the Head Light
days.summary: Wander the waterfront, then chase Maine's most famous lighthouse.

item.title: Explore the Old Port
item.blurb: Cobblestone streets of indie shops, roasters, and galleries — good for trinkets and souvenirs.

item.title: Portland Head Light & Fort Williams Park

location.name: Portland Head Light
location.address: 12 Captain Strout Cir, Cape Elizabeth, ME

item.blurb: Commissioned by George Washington and standing since 1791 — the classic Maine postcard, with cliff walks around the fort.

days.label: Day 26 — Casco Bay
days.summary: Out onto the water among the islands.

item.title: Casco Bay mailboat cruise
item.blurb: Ride the working mailboat run through the Calendar Islands — seals, lighthouses, and lobster boats.

rest.label: The rest of the day is yours
rest.note: You have been moving since Boston. Portland is a good town to stop moving in — the Old Port is four blocks of brick and cobblestone, there is a beer in it with your name on it, and the evening light on the water is the reason people paint here.

days.label: Day 27 — Art & Food
days.summary: A great small museum and a proper eating day.

item.title: Portland Museum of Art
item.blurb: Winslow Homer, Wyeth, and a strong American and Maine collection.

item.title: Old Port food crawl
item.blurb: Eventide oysters, Duckfat's duck-fat fries, and a Holy Donut — Portland's greatest hits.

days.label: Day 28 — Inland to the capital
days.summary: Leave the coast for Maine's capital on the Kennebec.

commute.scenicNote: North on I-95 into the interior — the coast gives way to river towns.
